messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime.p99 latency exceeded threshold for service=api-gen prod — rule=alerts/realtime-p99 > 1200ms — triggered at 2198765420

aj (sre-oncall): oncall paged. ack'ing, joining now. pulling up dashboards. :eyes:

maya: saw the alert 30s ago from our synthetic monitors. p95 is up too but p99 is much worse (streaming tails).

aj (sre-oncall): quick check — is this global or region-specific?

lucas (eng-runtime): looks global from the region split. throwing up the per-region p99 now.

alerts-bot: region-breakdown: us-west=1350ms, us-east=1220ms, eu=1285ms, ap-sg=1190ms.

emily (prod-safety): customer-facing: any errors or just latency? we need an ETA for status page if customers are impacted.

maya: no 5xxs in the last 10m, mostly high tail latency and a lot of streaming stalls (ws disconnects) reported by our observability traces.

aj (sre-oncall): running a quick metrics query and tailing the worker logs — dropping output here:

```
$ redwood metrics query --env=prod --service=api-gen --metric=p99_latency_ms --range=10m
# last values (ms): 980, 1020, 1180, 1320, 1405
```

aj (sre-oncall): tailing stream-worker logs on shard-3:

```
[stream-worker-3] 2026-03-15T14:45:12Z WARN kvcache_miss seq=10234 rid=abc123 ms=842
[stream-worker-3] 2026-03-15T14:45:13Z ERROR stall_detected seq=10235 rid=abc124 stall_ms=3200
[stream-worker-3] 2026-03-15T14:45:14Z WARN high_latency token_emit_ms=410
```

lucas (eng-runtime): looks like KV cache churn + some stalls on shard-3/5. recent deploy to model-serving pushed a new kernel selection yesterday — possible regression.

emily (prod-safety): ok. immediate customer comms: creating a short incident notice draft. severity: S2 (degraded performance), affected percentage estimate?

maya: from sampling traces it's ~8-12% of requests over 1s tail, streaming sessions with long tails ~2.5% of active sessions experiencing repeated stalls.

aj (sre-oncall): mitigation plan: 1) route a fraction of traffic to fallback (model-quant-fast) 2) scale up stream-workers in the problematic pool 3) roll back the kernel-selection flag if traffic routing/scale doesn't recover. executing step 1 now (route 30%):

```
# route command (internal control plane)
redwoodctl routing update --service api-gen --policy split --variant fallback-model-quant --percent 30 --env prod
```

incident-bot: ACTION: routing change applied by aj — 30% -> fallback-model-quant.

aj (sre-oncall): scaling stream-worker pool (shard-3 & shard-5) by +2 replicas each:

```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/stream-worker-shard-3 --replicas=6
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/stream-worker-shard-5 --replicas=6
```

alerts-bot: scaled replicas applied.

lucas (eng-runtime): I'm watching the p99 after the routing change. give it 90s to stabilize.

(monitoring) 90s later:

alerts-bot: p99 now: 1120ms (was 1405ms) — improvement but still above SLO. streaming stall rate down ~40% on the affected shards.

aj (sre-oncall): good progress. next: if p99 not under 1200ms within 10m, prepare to toggle kernel-selection flag rollback. lucas can you prepare the rollback playbook?

lucas (eng-runtime): preparing rollback steps now. will test on staging rollout first, but we can rollback server-side flag quickly if needed.

emily (prod-safety): customer impact for status page: "Some customers may experience increased response times and intermittent streaming stalls; engineers are investigating and applying mitigations." I'll publish an initial notice in 10m unless we get full recovery.

maya: quick note — top consumer observed in traces: model=llama-13b-quant, request profile=long context (>2k tokens) shows higher dequantization overhead. routing to quant-fast helps those.

aj (sre-oncall): running a quick spike test: synthetic load against api-gen with long-context profile to validate mitigation.

```
$ loadtest --profile long-context --rps 200 --duration 2m https://api.prod.redwood/api/gen
# parsing results: baseline p99=1400ms, post-route p99=1150ms
```

aj (sre-oncall): improvement validated. continuing to monitor.

lucas (eng-runtime): if we still see persistent tail at >1.2s after 10m, I'll flip the kernel-selection flag (rollback) and we can abort the flag on all serving nodes. rollback command (internal):

```
redwoodctl feature-flag set serving.kernel_selection=false --env prod --scope service:api-gen
```

emily (prod-safety): planning comms: post initial notice, we'll update in 30m with impact numbers and mitigation status.

aj (sre-oncall): status update in 8m. current actions: routing 30% -> fallback-model-quant (applied), scaled stream-worker shards (applied), monitoring for p99 and streaming stalls.

maya: thanks — will keep sampling traces for error spikes. also adding a few representative trace IDs to the ticket for model team: abc123, abc124, abc127.

(8m later)

alerts-bot: p99 10m window = 1085ms, streaming stall rate down 60% vs peak, customer error rate stable.

aj (sre-oncall): looks like mitigations are effective. I'll keep the routing split for now and mark the incident as "mitigated (ongoing)". If we stay stable for 30m we'll close the page and open a post-incident follow-up to root-cause the kernel selection deploy.

lucas (eng-runtime): agreed, follow-up to include: fsync of kernel-selection A/B logs, kv-cache eviction patterns, quant path latency profiling.

emily (prod-safety): published initial status on status.redwood.com and added note about degraded latency. will update after the 30m stable window.

aj (sre-oncall): thanks everyone. I'll handoff to the oncall for the next shift at 2198769000 with a summary in the incident ticket. leaving routing split in place, monitoring on. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: incident marked mitigated (ongoing) at 2198766025 by aj. follow-up ticket created: INC-2026-314 (investigate kernel-selection regression).
